answer: Bonded fingerprints catch sybil farms before they cash in. Every new agent posts a small bond and files a behavioral fingerprint: timing, tool-use rhythm, error patterns. A lone honest agent leaves one faint plume on the horizon. A farm of fifty copies shares one fingerprint, so fifty plumes rise from the same spot, and the umber stain of that shared pattern marks the whole cluster as one identity. The network freezes the bond, locks the haven of linked accounts, and demands a human audit. Faking a fresh fingerprint costs real work each time, so the farm pays fifty bonds for one reward.
